inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. Justice Sumeet Goel ruled that cancellation required clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances. Dismissing a plea seeking cancellation of pre-arrest bail in a house [...]
inputs.modified_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court is right that an accusation alone cannot erase the presumption of liberty. But pre-arrest bail is a serious safeguard, not a free pass: when stolen property has not been recovered, the interests of those harmed deserve more than a passing mention. Justice Sumeet Goel says cancellation requires clear proof of misuse of liberty or changed circumstances. That standard protects against punishment before trial, but it must not become an excuse to ignore evidence or leave victims carrying the cost of a system more attentive to the accused than to accountability.

rationales.entity_drift: The court and judge remain central; victims and the accused are added as actors in the commentary.
rationales.relation_drift: The cancellation standard is substantially preserved, but the modified text adds a normative claim that victims’ interests deserve consideration and omits the explicit holding that non-recovery or allegation seriousness alone is insufficient.
rationales.contradiction_drift: The modified text’s criticism and endorsement of the standard can coexist; it contains no clear internal contradiction.
